propositions: The byte-equivalence test executes Pandoc twice per unit (884 subprocesses total) with both production _convert and copied _legacy_convert sharing mutable _PANDOC_TO constants, coupling the oracle instead of providing independent verification.
Mutating production _PANDOC_TO to plain changes both production and copied oracle digests identically, proving the legacy copy is not an independent expected output but a coupled live execution.

Replacing the copied _legacy_convert subprocess invocation with immutable golden fixture lookup eliminates 884 redundant Pandoc spawns while preserving all 884 real production conversions and maintaining independent byte-equivalence validation.

The golden fixture must record exact generator Pandoc version (3.6.1) and binary SHA-256 fingerprint (94ebf1efbce3561379e8f25de3efe5aeabee64dc36dd8e8b9e96cf05b4195c52) with a deterministic regeneration command and runtime drift assertion to enable future maintenance.
